brief.headline: Push for 45-day terms (worth ₹2.68 L freed cash) and qualify Manjushree as second source — Kilitch is fragile (2/10 health, grey-zone) and 100% reseller, so we must secure supply before any price squeeze.

priceAsk.summary: Hold price for now; test maker-direct quotes from Manjushree and Mold-Tek once qualified
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to ₹0.65–0.80/pc (the lower end of the market ask band ₹0.55–1.20/pc) at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: Kilitch is 100.0% a trader — their price carries a reseller margin. The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. Once we qualify a manufacturer (Manjushree or Mold-Tek), we remove that margin and target the lower band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 45 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹2.68 L of cash for us (15 extra days). If we can stretch to 60 days, we free ₹5.36 L total.

brief.financialLeverage: Kilitch is fragile: money-health 2/10, grey-zone (Altman-Z 1.58), one legal case pending, and they keep only 2.8% profit on every ₹100 sold. But they already take 105 days to pay their own suppliers (peers take 57), so they're used to long payment cycles — asking for 45 or 60 days is fair. We're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue (₹65.27 L/yr) — a meaningful customer — but don't lean hard on price yet: their thin margin and weak health mean a big cut could break supply. Win on terms first, then qualify a second source before any pricing pressure.

evidence.point: Kilitch is 100% a trader — their price includes a reseller margin we can cut out by going direct to a maker
Market ask for 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume
We're a big customer — our ₹65.27 L spend is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue
They already take 105 days to pay their suppliers, far longer than similar firms (57 days), so asking for 45–60 days is reasonable
Money-health score is very weak at 2/10, and they're in the grey distress zone (Altman-Z 1.58)
They keep only 2.8% of every ₹100 they sell as profit — very thin margin, so a big price cut risks supply

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue), health B (65/100), makes pharma bottles and caps — top second-source candidate and removes the trader margin.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue), health B (73/100), strong in pharma containers — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: Kilitch's 2/10 health score and grey-zone flag mean supply could wobble — don't put all our eggs here; start qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
One pending legal case adds uncertainty — ask for details and monitor before increasing our dependence.
They're 100% a trader, so any cost shock (resin spike, supplier squeeze) hits them fast with no buffer — another reason to line up a maker-direct source.
Pushing price hard now (given the 2.8% margin) could tip them into real trouble and cut off our supply — win on payment terms first, then pivot to price once we have a second source locked.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and to keep growing our ₹65 lakh spend with you we'd like to move to 45-day terms — you already run 105 days with your own suppliers, so this should work smoothly for both sides.
